title: Meaning-as-Code (MAC) — formal schema v0.1.19-develop
description: The strict, machine-checkable contract for MAC YAML files across the four layers (Concept, Rules, Edges, Physical/Tables). The CORE vocabulary is closed: unknown keys are rejected, and there is NO extension namespace: `x-` is BANNED (operator ruling 2026-10-05) and tools/check_extension_keys.py refuses any such key as MAC012. Where an extension seems needed, that is a MAC gap — name the wall and change this schema. This schema is the normative companion to FRAMEWORK.md (the why) and CONCEPT_SPEC.md (the prose reference); where they disagree, FRAMEWORK.md governs intent and this schema governs syntax. Schema (schema_version) changes are recorded in CONFORMANCE.md §changelog; current generation v0.1.19-develop (adds the OPTIONAL typed-rule `subject` field — a short email-subject-style headline per rule, complementing `why`; additive over v0.1.12, so 0.1.12 files remain valid). Prior: v0.1.12 (adds the relationAliasBlock $def, the business-edge type `shared_attribute`, and the OPTIONAL edge.resolved_by / edge.aliases fields — giving a business relation a first-class NL-trigger alias slot resolved by mac.canon.relation_alias_resolve; additive over v0.1.11, so 0.1.11 files remain valid). Prior: v0.1.11 (adds the OPTIONAL concept.identity block {kind ∈ mac.concept.identity, canonical_key} — declaring a concept's canonical identity; additive over v0.1.10, so 0.1.10 files remain valid). Prior: v0.1.10 (adds the aliasBlock $def: an optional two-tier `aliases` map — scope_relative + multilingual — on the enumeration shape, resolved by mac.canon.alias_resolve; additive over v0.1.9's content-model UDF seam, so 0.1.9 files remain valid during migration). v0.1.14: the `^x-` escape hatch is CLOSED. It had stood in 58 places, written as `patternProperties: {"^x-": true}` — `true` meaning any shape, any type, no validation — so every `additionalProperties: false` in this file was immediately undone beside it. Extension keys were therefore not violations of MAC; MAC SANCTIONED them, and what they held could not be checked. Measured on the day x-grain was retired: two of four declared cell keys were false while still reading as VERIFIED, and the two that held were the two a view enforced. Where an extension seems needed, that is a MAC gap — name the wall and change the schema, which is now the only way to add a field.
$comment: A MAC file is one of four file types, distinguished by its discriminator key: concept files have 'concept:', rules files 'rules:', edges files 'edges:', table files 'table:'. A validator selects the matching $def by file location; the root oneOf also resolves it structurally.

AttributeItem.description: v0.5 cross-class — an EAV / enum-constrained attribute (reference / entity). Distinct from PropertyItem (primitive): an attribute's values must belong to an enumeration (`value_domain`) and are typically read from an EAV column.

value_domain.description: the enumeration the attribute's values belong to

source.description: WHICH DATA SOURCE this ontology is for, as the project declares it (`a worked bundle`). An ontology is bound to one source — its relations, its columns, its grain — and this is the binding stated in one place. It scopes every rule in the file: a rule's own `scope` defaults to it. Required.

version.description: The CONCEPT's version, bumped by whoever changes its meaning. Not the schema's version and not the bundle's: it answers "has this notion changed since I last read it". Measured on the worked bundle: 16 concepts at 1.0 and one at 1.1, which is what a version looks like when it is maintained rather than stamped.

schema_version.description: Which generation of mac.schema.json this file is written against. It is what lets a reader know a key's absence is a vintage rather than an omission, and what a migration selects on. Stamp the schema's own `version`, not a guess. Required.

provenance.description: How this object came to be: harvested = emitted by the harvest (self-documenting); authored/tuned = MANUAL work, which MUST carry an entry in interventions/ledger.yaml (check_intervention_ledger.py).

profiled_via.description: How the raw source was profiled, in a note — 'catalogue metadata plus a live column profile'. Distinct from `provenance`, which is the harvested / authored / tuned protocol stamp: this says what was LOOKED AT, that says how the file came to exist. Keep the example in nouns every engine has; a core-grammar example that names a vendor's product makes the grammar specific to it.

metadata.description: THE FILE'S OWN IDENTITY CARD — who wrote it, against which schema, for which source, and how far it has been taken. It says nothing about MEANING: everything here would still be true if the concept meant something else entirely. That is the split worth holding, because a question is answered from `concept`, `grounding` and `contract`, and never from here. Required. THREE KEYS REMOVED 2026-10-05, each measured across the worked bundle's 17 concepts: `concept` DUPLICATED `concept.name` 17 of 17 and was only ever read as a fallback behind it; `status` was the constant 'draft' on all 17, so the one check reading it could not discriminate (it appended a clause to a MAC006 witness, never decided it); `owner` was the constant 'operator' and reached only a display row. A field with one value bundle-wide is not per-concept metadata.

name.description: PascalCase ontology id — the single canonical identifier.

label.description: The concept's name AS A READER SAYS IT, where that differs from its identifier. `Color` is the key, `Colour` is the label. It is what a projection prints and what an answer calls the thing, so it carries spelling, case and local usage that an identifier cannot.

class.description: WHAT KIND OF THING THIS CONCEPT IS — the closed five-term vocabulary mac_vocabulary.yaml#concept.class declares (this enum is landed from it by tools/check_vocabulary_parity.py --write and is not edited by hand). Shrunk from seven on 2026-10-05: `reference` was RENAMED `entity` (the old name is taken one plane down by concept.column.identity.reference, which means a POINTER AT a thing), and `meta` was dropped — it was admitted here but absent from mac-runtime's ConceptClass, so a concept writing it validated and then failed to load. `grouping` was proposed for removal and KEPT: this schema makes `members.over` mandatory for it and the console draws the containment channel from that.

definition.description: WHAT THIS NOTION IS, in prose, for a person — the one field in the file that a reader with no schema can use. Say what it is, at what grain, READ FROM THE ROWS rather than from the table name, and say what it is NOT where a neighbour could be mistaken for it. It is also the text a model is shown when choosing between two concepts, so a definition that omits the distinction between two readings is how the wrong one gets picked. Measurement belongs here: "681.72 net against 717.60 gross on one sale" settles an ambiguity that an adjective cannot.

notes.description: Working remarks a reader may need and the definition should not carry — an open uncertainty, a measurement that justifies a choice, a thing checked and ruled out. Nothing here is normative: a statement that must hold is a rule with a body, and a statement that must be READ is part of the definition. If a note starts telling the engine what to do, it is in the wrong field.

concept.description: THE MEANING ITSELF — what this notion IS, independently of where it is stored. Name, label, class, definition, identity, semantics. Nothing in this block names a relation or a column; that is `grounding`, and the separation is the whole point of the framework: the same meaning can be re-grounded on a different warehouse without a word of it changing. Required.

properties.description: Intrinsic PRIMITIVE attributes — each a cross-class PropertyItem {name,type,required,doc}. Concept-typed relations are edges, not properties.

members.description: grouping rollup (over + member sets — see groupingMembers) OR a legacy containment list (whole→part).

derived_by_rule.description: marks a concept whose value is produced by a rule; the formula lives in rules.yaml (single-homing), this only names it.

allOf.$comment: v0.5 per-class template — enumeration: the value set lives in `values:` (one concept = one set). The `enumerations:` plural wrapper of the v0.5 content model was RETIRED 2026-09-29 with the rest of that model (no reader on either side); the `not: required` clause that policed it went with it.
v0.5 per-class template — measure: must declare per-axis additivity (the footgun-preventer).

then.$comment: v0.1.15: a measure declares WHAT IT IS (`measure_type`) and WHAT ITS AXES ARE (`axis_kinds`); the per-axis `additivity` block is DERIVED from those two by the law in mac_vocabulary.yaml#concept.column.measure_type and is no longer required here. A concept that writes it as well states the same fact twice — and because it authored both the premise and the conclusion, the two could drift: a target-inventory measure declared `Target` and wrote `geography: additive`, which the law forbids, and a value anchor summed it across products on the strength of it. You cannot contradict a value you do not write. Precedent: `values` carries no `required` either — a closed set may delegate its members to a register and check_enumeration_closure honours that rather than demanding a copy.

allOf.$comment: v0.5 per-class template — grouping: must roll up a leaf via the members template (over + member_source / definitions).

ConnectionFile.description: THE CONNECTION ENVELOPE (the file named by mac.project.yaml#runtime.connection). THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS DEFINITION IS THE LINE IT DRAWS: MAC reads the whole manifest and exactly three keys of THIS file — who the connector is (from the manifest), how the credential is obtained (`credentials`), and where the connector's own payload begins (`config`). Everything past that line is the connector's. The grammar therefore does NOT learn what a region, a workgroup or a catalog is, and could not be made to: those nouns have no home above `config`, whose contents this schema deliberately does not describe. `additionalProperties: false` is the load-bearing half — it is what leaves `aws_secret_access_key:` nowhere legal to sit, and what forces every vendor key DOWN into `config` where a named party owns its meaning. This file is DEPLOYMENT, not bundle: it is overridable (connection.local.yaml, $DEPLOYMENT_CONFIG) and therefore may never say which CODE runs — `runtime.connector` lives in the manifest precisely because an override chain must be able to change where you point, never what loads into the host process.

spec_version.description: The connector-protocol generation, and the DISCRIMINATOR that makes this definition safe to apply. A connection file WITHOUT it is the legacy flat shape (measured live in this estate: `engine, region, workgroup, output, catalog, view_database, view_schema, glue_databases, credentials, account` at the top level) and belongs to the compatibility reader, for exactly one spec version; the gate reports the legacy count as a DENOMINATOR, not a failure. Required here so that a legacy file mis-routed to this definition fails with one legible error naming the missing version rather than nine confusing unknown-key errors — and so that an EMPTY file fails at all, which is a stated reject class (MAC002) it would otherwise pass by carrying no forbidden key.

credentials.description: Deliberately NOT in `required`: a connector needing no credential omits the block entirely, which is the DuckDB case and is the honest spelling of 'no credential required'. Requiring it would force every credential-free bundle to write `{mode: none}`, i.e. to restate a fact its own absence already states.

config.description: OPAQUE TO MAC. THIS IS THE DELEGATION LINE, and the one object in this grammar that is deliberately left open. Validated not by this schema but by the JSON Schema the CONNECTOR ships, resolved from sdk/connector/index.json — which is the distinction that separates this from the `x-` extension keys the framework ruled out: an `x-` key was checked by NOBODY, whereas `config` is checked by a named party's schema, and when that party is absent MAC prints what went UNCHECKED with its denominator and withholds the claim that depended on it, rather than reporting a clean run over nothing. Describing these keys here — region, workgroup, catalog and their kin — is precisely the failure this definition exists to prevent: it would put one vendor's nouns into the canon and make every new engine a schema bump. TWO HONEST LIMITS, recorded rather than hidden: (1) the residual secret scan over this block is AWS-shaped by construction, so for the non-AWS engines this seam exists to enable it catches nothing — the structural guarantee lives in `credentials` above, and only there; (2) JSON Schema expresses most cross-field rules and not all, so a rule it cannot express is not silently skipped but belongs to the connector's own validate_config(), which runs at publish and at answer, and the mount tier says which tier it reached.

label.description: A human name for this deployment target, for disclosure lines. Carries no meaning a gate reads.

note.description: Free prose about this deployment. Deliberately unstructured: it is the pressure valve that keeps operational commentary out of the keys a gate reads.

to.description: NULL, always. Not a guess and not an omission: no parent relation exists.

basis.description: on what this was detected. WEAKER evidence than a measurement against a parent, because there is no parent to measure against — a bundle with no naming convention gets no dangling detection at all, and that must read as 'not detectable here', never as 'none exist'.

DataPlaneApprovalFile.description: THE DATA PIPELINE'S DECLARED EXIT — a named human's sign-off that this bundle's dataset configuration is approved, and the one artifact in a bundle that NO AGENT MAY WRITE: the ontology guard denies every governed write to this path unconditionally, and no unlock marker lifts it, because an unlock the agent can also satisfy is not a gate. FLAT SCALARS ONLY, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: the PreToolUse guard must read this file, it is copied into.claude/hooks/ with no import path, and it FAILS CLOSED on a protected path — so a PyYAML import error in it would deny every edit in the repository. The guard therefore parses this file with ~20 lines of standard library, and sdk/gate + tools/check_guard_seam.py prove that parser and yaml.safe_load agree over every shape. Nesting here would break that, which is why additionalProperties is false and every value is a scalar. The write stamp reuses the question-ledger vocabulary rather than inventing one: submitted_via must be `human` (an agent may write a DESCRIPTION; only a human may write a DISPOSITION) and identity_basis distinguishes a verified sign-in from a locally declared identity, so a weaker approval reads as weaker rather than as equal. `covers` names EVERY registered issue id: the threshold is per-issue human acknowledgement and no wildcard is permitted. `digest` says WHICH data plane was approved — recomputed from the files on every run, so an approval is a statement about one state and not a permanent licence.

id.description: the reserved sign-off id. `s.` is the sign-off prefix the question ledger already uses.

status.description: applying is a human developer act; a draft is not an approval.

verdict.description: what the human said about the plane they were asked to ratify. Only `confirmed` opens the ontology pipeline.

covers.description: EVERY registered issue id, comma- or space-separated. No wildcard: the count of uncovered ids must be 0 and cannot move unless a person names the specific thing. If that is too many ids, the fix is a coarser REGISTER, never a coarser gate.

lock.description: the reviewable per-file digest sibling. EVIDENCE, never AUTHORITY: it lives outside the protected set and is agent-writable by design, because it is what the operator diffs. Forging it buys nothing — the gate computes the roll-up from the FILES and compares it to `digest` here, so the lock is never the compared value.

decision.description: the durable decision record, decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md. The gate fails when it names no file that exists.

by.description: the named person or role who approved — never "the team", never a tool.

identity_basis.description: verified = a signed-in identity. local-declared = the identity the person who started a local server declared; NOT authentication, and shown as weaker. `imported` is deliberately absent: a sign-off written by an importer ratifies nothing.

submitted_via.description: an agent may write a DESCRIPTION; only a human may write a DISPOSITION. Rejecting the honestly-stamped agent case is what makes the dishonest one a lie rather than a shortcut.

DataQualityRegisterFile.description: DQ findings on the RAW plane, each graded and owned. Authored by the data-plane harvest, which is why every finding carries `confidence` (C=measured live, cite the number; I=inferred; Q=needs-SME) and an `sme_owner` naming what that person must ratify — the doubt channel that existed here long before concept authoring had one.

items.description: CLOSED v0.1.15, and widened to describe the GENERATED register as well as a hand-authored one. It required [id, title, finding] and declared only the hand-authored fields, while `mac_dq_findings` has been writing measurement / needs / status / ruled_by / raised_by all along — accepted in silence because `additionalProperties` was unset, and the required `finding` was missing without complaint because MAC002 was never computed. Both halves are now true at once.

needs.description: What must happen for this finding to close — for a generated finding, the one-line form of the prepared ruling below.

ruling.description: A PREPARED RULING, to CORE.md §6: a closed question, its permitted answers, what was established with evidence, what only a human can settle, the consequence of EACH answer, and a recommendation — or an explicit statement that the measurement does not lean and why. Added v0.1.15 so a console can offer the answers as buttons rather than a text box.

status.description: The DISPOSITION, which survives re-measurement: the measurement is refreshed, the ruling is not.

EdgeEndpoint.description: an edge endpoint is a CONCEPT, never a raw view/table. It names the concept at this end; the physical relation lives in that concept's grounding plus the edge's join_rule/realized_by. Authoring an endpoint as a `view`/`key` is FORBIDDEN (additionalProperties:false rejects them): a join between stored relations that is not a join between concepts is a pipeline transform, not an ontology edge. This is what keeps edges at the semantic stage and out of the data/pipeline stage. v0.1.18: an endpoint is FULLY DEFINED or it is not an endpoint — `concept` AND `cardinality` are both required. An endpoint that names a concept and promises nothing about how many partners a row finds is half an edge: the projectors then supply the missing half themselves, silently (see `cardinality`).

source.description: the source/ontology this concept belongs to (enables cross-source federation edges).

concept.description: REQUIRED — the concept at this end of the edge.

ref.description: pointer to the concept definition (path#anchor), resolved cross-file by the referential gate.

role.description: the relationship role/name read from this end (typically on `from`): e.g. placedBy, measuredForCountry.

cardinality.description: REQUIRED on BOTH ends — how many partners a row at the other end finds here. `1` exactly one (every key resolves AND finds at most one) · `0..1` at most one (may resolve nothing, must never find two) · `1..N` every key resolves, fan-out unbounded · `0..N` promises nothing, so nothing can contradict it. CLOSED, and the set is a MEASUREMENT of what the framework can actually judge and draw, not a taste: these four are the intersection of every live consumer's map (sdk/project/er_model.py CARDINALITY, tools/mac_to_shacl.py CARD, tools/mac_to_mermaid.py CARD_L/CARD_R, tools/check_edge_joins_measured.py EXACTLY_ONE/AT_MOST_ONE) and they are also exactly the four values the estate's edges use across all of their endpoints. WHY `1..1` AND `N` ARE REFUSED THOUGH THEY READ AS LEGAL: both are synonyms of a value already here (`1..1` = `1`, `N` = `0..N`) and both are SILENTLY MIS-RENDERED rather than rejected by a projector that meets them — mac_to_shacl defaults an unmapped value to (minCount 0, maxCount 1), so a declared `1..1` ships as `at most one`, weaker than the claim; mac_to_mermaid defaults the left terminal to `||`, so a declared `N` is DRAWN as exactly one, the opposite of the claim. Admitting a token that no judge reads and two projectors quietly rewrite is the silent-default class this requirement exists to close. `N..N` is in no consumer map, no bundle and no proposal, so it is refused outright. WIDENING THIS SET IS ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO: the pending table-link proposal (C5) adds `1..1` and `N` TOGETHER WITH the judges that would then read them; adding them here first would put the token in the grammar and leave it judged by nothing. AND THE VALUE IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CHOICE: sharpen `0..N` to `1` only with a measurement, and cite it in `verified_by`/`realized_by` rather than retyping the number.

planned_edges.description: a PROMOTION CANDIDATE, and DELIBERATELY NOT AN EDGE. A planned edge's whole content is the ABSENCE of a declarable endpoint — 'no join exists to declare' — so the endpoint rules that govern `edges[]` (an EdgeEndpoint at each end, a cardinality on both) STOP HERE, and applying them would turn every entry in the estate red for having correctly declared nothing. What DOES carry across is the one rule that is about nameability rather than about joins: an entry must have an `edge_id`, because a candidate nothing can name is a candidate nothing can cite or promote. Before this version the array had no item schema at all, so an entry could be any value whatever.

edge_id.description: REQUIRED — the id this candidate will keep when it is promoted to an edge, so the decision that promotes it names the same thing the plan did.

business_relation_minted_as.description: the business edge id this candidate will be minted as, when the promoted physical edge and the business relation are not the same name.

blocked_by.description: WHAT IS MISSING, not that something is. A candidate blocked for no stated reason is indistinguishable from one nobody worked out.

measured_reference.description: bundle-relative path to the physical-plane reference file that measured the candidate key. This is where the evidence LIVES; the `evidence` string below quotes it and does not replace it.

reference_id.description: the id of the entry in that references file, so the quote can be checked against its source.

evidence.description: the measurement, WITH ITS DENOMINATORS, quoted from `measured_reference`.

becomes_an_edge_when.description: REQUIRED IN PRACTICE, not in the grammar: the condition whose arrival turns this candidate into an edge. Absent, a planned edge is a wish with an id.

items.description: v0.5: edge type must be LEGAL for its level. Illegal types 'denormalized' and 'literal_equal' were removed (denormalized → not an edge; literal_equal → value_mapped_key). v0.1.18: `edge_id` is REQUIRED. An edge nothing can name is an edge nothing can cite — `@join:` dereferences `edge:<edge_id>`, a rule and a decision record refer to an edge by it, and `realized_by`/`verified_by` are how it cites its evidence. It is also already load-bearing and failing in the WRONG PLACE: tools/protosql_render.py indexes edges by id and silently DROPS one that has none, so `@join:` then reports `edge-not-found` and blames the caller for a defect in the edge; the runtime synthesises a POSITIONAL id instead, which silently renames when edges are reordered. Requiring it moves that refusal to the grammar, where the author can see it.

verified_by.description: (additive) a resolvable ref (path.yaml#id) to a data expectation that proves this edge's cardinality/1:1 claim. Referentially resolved by check_references.py against the expectations file's ids; dangling → referential error. A string ref, distinct from realized_by (a canon binding) and resolved_by (a resolution-rule anchor).

resolved_by.description: v0.1.12 (additive): a ref/anchor (path.yaml#anchor) to the resolution rule that computes a business relation's instance set — e.g. the self-relation of a shared_attribute edge. A string anchor, distinct from realized_by (a canon binding). Used by a level:business type:shared_attribute edge in place of realized_by.

aliases.description: v0.1.12 (additive): the first-class NL trigger vocabulary for a business relation — surfaces resolve to THIS EDGE (by edge_id) via a deterministic token→relation resolver (mac.canon.relation_alias_resolve). Optional; absent ⇒ no relation-alias resolution for this edge.

allOf.$comment: v0.1.18: a PHYSICAL edge is REALISED or it is nothing. The two BUSINESS branches above already require a realisation — identity must carry `realized_by`, shared_attribute must carry `resolved_by` — and the physical branch constrained only the TYPE, so a physical edge could name two concepts and a cardinality while saying nothing about how the relationship is reached, and validate. Eight did, for a day, after a ruling correctly DELETED their join predicates (the join fanned out 215x) and left nothing behind. The reasoning went into a YAML comment, which no gate can read, so 'no join is needed here' and 'nobody has worked this out' became one absence — and a renderer cannot tell those apart either. A physical edge must now say which: a join predicate, a column that carries it, or a rule/transform that resolves it.

ImpurityResolutionMapFile.description: which TRANSFORM resolves which DQ finding, and the guarantee the ontology may then rely on. The join between the quality plane and the transformation plane — without it a finding and its fix are two facts nobody relates, and the ontology cannot tell which impurities it may stop defending against.

InterventionLedgerFile.description: the APPEND-ONLY record of manual work — which objects a human or agent authored, tuned or retired, and why. Autodiscovered output is self-documenting (the descriptor IS the record); manual work is not, and an implicit object is not a protocol. Read by MAC010 (change-unprotocolled), which means the framework already DEPENDED on this file while having no definition for it.

KnowledgeSectionsFile.description: SOURCE KNOWLEDGE extracted VERBATIM from a vendor document, sliced on the document's own heading numbering and carrying the source hash. The documents stay out of reach by design; what is published is what they SAY, quoted and attributed, so a reader can challenge a claim without being handed the PDF. Verbatim is not stylistic — it makes the register mechanically verifiable, which is impossible once someone has paraphrased.

LineageFile.description: data/lineage/lineage.json — WHERE EVERY SERVED COLUMN CAME FROM, measured from the view SQL by mac_lineage.py. THE ONE LINEAGE ARTIFACT: a second producer (lineage_project.py) once built a rival set of flows from a `consumes` map nothing generates, found no column edges, and labelled every column a derived CONSTANT — which is what the console rendered. Collapsed to this file on 2026-09-28 on the operator's ruling that two artifacts for one fact is 'one too many'. It had no definition here until the artifact-conformance gate asked, on its first run, why a structured artifact was routed to nothing.

columns.description: One entry per served column. It names a SOURCE (source_relation + source_column) or carries an EXPRESSION — those are the two honest answers. An entry with neither is a column nobody can explain, and check_lineage_coverage fails the dataset for it.

expression.description: the arithmetic, when the column is computed

id.description: keyed by RELATION AND COLUMN on BOTH ends. Two references can join one pair of relations on different columns; an id derived from the relation pair alone collides, and a renderer that identifies a line by id then cannot tell them apart — one silently stops responding to selection.

from.description: the CHILD relation: the one carrying the referencing column.

to.description: the PARENT relation: the one whose measured key column is referenced.

parent_key_role.description: identity = the parent's WHOLE measured key, so the reference names ONE ROW. key_part = one column of a composite key, so it names a VALUE SET. Conflating them draws a crow's foot that says something the data does not.

verdict.description: `broken_reference` added v0.1.15: between near_miss and rejected — the child USES the parent's real key values and the overlap is not interval arithmetic, so it is a relationship, and 4 % of the rows disobey it. NOT DRAWN, RAISED.

participation.description: NOT CARDINALITY. Three relations can all be one-to-many while one parent has 10 of 74 rows never referenced, another 52,801 of 104,990 and a third 0 of 2,517. Keys alone draw all three identically mandatory.

evidence.description: the exact counts the verdict was taken on. An absent count is NOT a zero — it means the reference was not measured.

name_match.description: A LABEL FOR A READER, never an input to a verdict. Name matching alone would propose 14 of 171 measured candidates on the reference bundle and miss 8 of its 17 drawn references.

ambiguous_with.description: other parents that measure IDENTICALLY. Both are recorded and neither is chosen: value inclusion genuinely cannot separate them, and picking one would be a fabrication dressed as a measurement.

PhaseFile.description: the rule-governance phase switch. BUILD = ontology CRUD permitted and a missing lock is GREEN; TUNE = default-DENY, where any un-blessed delta reds the gate and the agent PROPOSES rather than edits. Only the operator flips it. A bundle sitting in BUILD is not governed, and that is a fact worth being able to read mechanically.

frozen_at.description: When the phase was frozen. Read by tools/mac_to_explorer.py.

frozen_by.description: Who froze the phase. Read by tools/mac_to_explorer.py.

PipelineExit.description: What ENDING this pipeline means. THREE SHAPES, deliberately different, because confusing 'a tool said yes' with 'a person said yes' is the defect this whole block exists to prevent. `register` names the bundle-relative path of a data-quality register every one of whose issues must carry a terminal disposition — the DATA pipeline's exit since 2026-09-18, and the shape a new bundle declares. `approval` names the bundle-relative path of a separate human sign-off; it was the data pipeline's exit before that date and is kept because a bundle that already declares one must keep working. `gate`+`must_exit` names a machine verdict, for a pipeline whose completion a checker can decide. WHY `register` REPLACED `approval` AS THE SHAPE TO DECLARE: the separate file duplicated the register in a LESS informative form — one date and one name against N individually-argued dispositions — and the operator it was built for refused to sign it, having already ruled on every issue one at a time. WHAT THE COLLAPSE COSTS, stated rather than glossed: the sign-off path is one the ontology guard denies UNCONDITIONALLY, so an agent cannot write it; a register is agent-writable, so this exit rests on ATTRIBUTION (`ruled_by`, `reason`, git blame) and not on PREVENTION. Carried in mac_vocabulary.yaml#data_plane_gate.approval_missing and in the gate's own refusal text.

register.description: bundle-relative path to a DATA-QUALITY REGISTER whose every issue must carry a terminal `mac.dq_status` term with that term's own `requires:` met. An `open` issue, or an `accepted`/`wont_fix` naming nobody, leaves this exit UNREACHED and the ontology pipeline closed. The evidence is per-issue and individually argued, which is strictly more than one signature over a list of ids — and the file is agent-writable, so this exit rests on ATTRIBUTION rather than on a token no agent can reach. An approval file present alongside it is still honoured.

approval.description: bundle-relative path to a HUMAN SIGN-OFF. The ontology guard denies every governed write to this path unconditionally — no unlock marker lifts it — so an agent cannot satisfy this exit condition. SUPERSEDED by `register` as the shape a new bundle declares (2026-09-18) and still honoured wherever it appears: a bundle that carries a sign-off must not silently lose it.

gate.description: the command whose exit code decides this pipeline's completion — a MACHINE verdict, never a substitute for a human one.

must_exit.description: the exit code the gate must return.

ProfileFile.description: v0.1.14 (C10): everything MEASURED about one relation, in its own file under data/profiles/, written only by machine. WHY IT IS NOT IN THE DESCRIPTOR. The runtime inlines every data/datasets/*.yaml verbatim into its system block and keys its prompt cache on those files' size and mtime. Profiling rewrites a descriptor on EVERY run — `measured_at` always moves, by design — so each re-measurement invalidated the whole cache for a change no engine could observe. Measured before the split: 64,9 % of the descriptor bytes were profile, and of that 95,3 % was the value domain (which the reader does need, and which stays) against 4,7 % census (which it does not). It is also the R3 rule made physical: DESIGN FACTS (column role, the domain) are ruled once and live with the meaning; EVIDENCE rots and lives here. A human editing this file is a MAC002 error.

metadata.description: carries schema_version so the validator does not SKIP this file. A skipped file is an unvalidated one, which for a machine-written plane is the whole risk.

of.description: descriptor stem this measures. A profile whose descriptor is gone is a measurement of nothing.

profile.description: WHEN this relation was profiled and WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE THEN. Split deliberately from the design facts a reader authors: design facts are discovered once and do not rot, while EVIDENCE rots continuously — so a diff that touches only this block means the SOURCE moved, and a diff that touches the column roles means the DATA OBJECT changed shape and needs a fresh ruling. v_<source>_kpi.yaml claimed 'VERIFIED 2026-08-16 … 0 multi-row' for four days while the warehouse went to millions of doubled figures: the word VERIFIED in prose is a sentence, not a test.

measured_at.description: ISO-8601 with offset, when the scan ran

rows.description: exact row count at that moment

newest_write.description: the source's own high-water mark, where it has a write timestamp — this is what lets a later reader tell a stale measurement from a current one

method.description: the tool and version that produced this

columns.description: per-column census. Counts only — the value domain lives on the descriptor's column.

singletons.description: VALUES HELD BY EXACTLY ONE ROW. Measured by mac_profile.py/6 in one GROUPING SETS scan, only for near-unique non-key, non-numeric columns (>= 1,000 distinct and >= 1% of rows); ABSENT means the column was not a candidate, never that the count is zero. This is the measurement behind `rulings.never_axis: privacy` (reference_manual/column_rulings.md §4): a column most of whose values name one row is an identifier wearing a dimension's role, and GROUP BY it returns one row per person. mac_dq_findings.py raises DQ-IDENTIFYING-<relation>-<column> from it, and the ruling cites that id as `evidence`. Added 2026-09-29, operator: the ruling is a MUST HAVE, and a prohibition without a measurement is a preference.

determined_by.description: columns that FUNCTIONALLY DETERMINE this one. The distinction that matters and the one a discrimination test cannot see: a brand-code column is determined by `role` for the five brand perspectives — structural, a LAW — and separately by the market code, because every market code belongs to exactly one brand — a naming CONVENTION. A column redundant by convention must stay in a key; one redundant by law need not. Measured, not assumed.

identity_evidence.description: v0.1.14 (C3): the PROOF behind the column roles — machine-written, never hand-edited (a human editing it is a MAC002 error). The grain is a DESIGN FACT and lives on the columns as role/determined_by; this block is only the measurement that established it, and measurements rot. v_<source>_kpi.yaml claimed 'VERIFIED 2026-08-16 … 0 multi-row' for four days while the warehouse went to millions of doubled figures — the word VERIFIED is a sentence, not a test. A diff HERE means the SOURCE moved against a grain that still stands (a defect); a diff in the column roles means the OBJECT changed shape (a redesign, needing a fresh ruling).

source_watermark.description: the source's own high-water mark AT measurement — what the evidence is true OF. Without it a stale proof is indistinguishable from a fresh one.

measure.description: the column agreement was tested on. THE ONE BIT A HUMAN SUPPLIES; if it is wrong, every classification below it is confidently wrong with full evidence attached.

stratum.description: the slice measured, if not all of it

excluded.description: columns held OUT of the key search. Sometimes necessary: a concatenated surrogate (cycle_key = 'Brand|2025-12-11|Scenario 1') wins every greedy step by construction, and every atomic axis it encodes then reads DEAD.

key.description: the measured identity columns — the grain, DERIVED, not declared

delivery_axes.description: split rows, not figures; ruled by a human and recorded here

groups.description: groups remaining when this column is left out

split.description: of those, how many gained a second row

disagree.description: of those, how many carry DIFFERENT measure values. Splitting is not enough: a delivery axis splits too, and the halves AGREE, because they are the same figure twice.

columns.description: per candidate: what leaving it out did

ruled.description: columns a HUMAN placed in the key or the delivery axes, which the measurement could not settle. Named separately from `key` so the two halves stay distinguishable: everything else in `key` was derived, these were decided. A later re-measurement must not silently overwrite a ruling, and a reader must be able to see which columns rest on evidence and which on a judgement.

ProjectFile.description: THE BUNDLE MANIFEST (mac.project.yaml). Shape measured across three live manifests — only `planes` is universal, so it is the only required key; `additionalProperties: false` is kept deliberately, because an unenumerated manifest key is exactly the invention this definition exists to catch, and there is no extension namespace to fall back on. Previously the only bundle file MAC did not define — it was exempted by a hardcoded basename check inside validate_schema.py, which meant the file where a bundle declares its own conformance was itself unchecked. It no longer carries the three declarations that had nowhere legitimate to live: `profile` (CONFORMANCE.md §2 — what each x- key means; without it every x- key is undeclared debt by construction), `conformance.out_of_scope` (the MAC001 escape hatch — a bundle may own files MAC does not define, but it must SAY SO), and `reproduction` (how the bundle is rebuilt, as CHECKABLE data rather than prose that goes stale — measured twice on <dataset>'s REPRODUCTION.md). `profile` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT (2026-10-05). CONFORMANCE §2 described it as "the list of x- keys a project uses and what each means" — a declaration mechanism for the `x-` extension namespace, which is BANNED. No bundle has ever written it. The description used to claim this $def carried it while `additionalProperties: false` refused it, so the schema invited a key it then rejected.

spec_version.description: Absent on bundles predating the container spec; required going forward.

capabilities.description: Claims validated against real contents on Open; a claim the container cannot back fails.

planes.description: plane name -> directory. `data` and `ontology` are conventional; `governance` holds the control mechanisms (PHASE, lock, sme_ledger, properties, decisions, interventions) in ONE place rather than scattered across the bundle root.

runtime.description: WHAT THIS BUNDLE NEEDS IN ORDER TO BE ANSWERED FROM. Previously `{"type": "object"}` — no properties, no required, no additionalProperties — which is to say the manifest's runtime block was ungoverned, and an ungoverned object in the ONE file a bundle uses to declare its own conformance is exactly the hole this schema exists to close. The measured cost of leaving it open: `runtime: {conection:..., credentials: {mode: plaintext, value: hunter2xyz}}` validates CLEAN against the old shape (note the typo, silently accepted) and returns zero findings from check_bundle_secrets, because mac.project.yaml sits in that gate's config allowlist and the key is spelled `value`, not `password`. Closing the object is what makes a sixth key ARGUABLE rather than silent, and it is what leaves a credential nowhere to sit in the manifest — credentials belong in the connection envelope ($defs/ConnectionFile), which is deployment and overridable, never in the bundle manifest, which is not. MEASURED BEFORE CLOSING, because `additionalProperties: false` is the one non-additive edit here: across the 27 mac.project.yaml manifests reachable on this machine, 4 carry a `runtime:` block and their key universe is EXACTLY these five — source 4, connection 4, interpreter 3, model_catalog 3, connector 2 — with zero sixth key and every value a string. No key is `required`, because one of those four manifests carries only {source, connection, connector}: a bundle that declines a mechanism it has no use for must not be nagged for it. A bundle with no `runtime:` block at all remains well-formed, readable, renderable — and not answerable.

source.description: The bundle's own source key — the token its served relations are addressable by.

connector.description: WHICH CONNECTOR, and it lives HERE rather than in the connection file for one reason that decides the whole boundary: the connection file is overridable (connection.local.yaml is gitignored, $DEPLOYMENT_CONFIG is an arbitrary path from the environment), so putting the connector identity there would let an out-of-band file substitute the CODE that loads into the host process. An override chain must be able to change where you point, never what runs. Independently: which engine a bundle grounds on is a fact ABOUT THE BUNDLE, and the manifest alone should answer 'what does this bundle need?' without opening a file the bundle may not ship.

connection.description: The PATH to the connection envelope ($defs/ConnectionFile), relative to the bundle root. The path is the bundle's; everything the file then says about WHERE to point is the deployment's. A path that escapes the bundle root, or names a file that is not there, is a defect a gate owns — not something this type can express.

interpreter.description: Path to the bundle's interpreter document.

model_catalog.description: Path to the bundle's model catalog.

publish.description: WHAT A PUBLISHED COPY OF THIS BUNDLE CONTAINS. Was a bare `{type: object}` — so any key validated and none was documented; `include` has been read by sdk/cli/publish.py all along.

include.description: The paths a published copy carries. Read by sdk/cli/publish.py.

serving.description: THE BUNDLE'S SERVING CONTRACT — how this bundle spells the relations it serves. A CORE key, deliberately, and not an `x-` extension: the serving-name convention was the single most-replicated finding of the eight-walk ingestion experiment, and every walk that tried to declare it reached for `x-serving-naming`, which this schema rejects (additionalProperties:false, no ^x- pattern) and which tools/check_extension_keys.py PROHIBITS as MAC012. The framework was therefore teaching, in a gate's failure message, the one declaration two other mechanisms refuse — opposite policies in one framework, which is a defect to remove rather than a tension to document. Removing it means the convention must have a home the core defines, validates and a gate reads: this one. Enforced by tools/check_served_name_distinct.py.

naming.description: The serving-name convention THIS bundle keeps. Structural on purpose — a marker plus a role table, from which the gate DERIVES the acceptance test. It is deliberately NOT a free-text regex or name template: an unverifiable string is exactly the weakness that got `x-` keys ruled out, and a convention nothing can check is worse than none, because the manifest then claims a guarantee nothing enforces. Declaring this block makes the full build-shape `<role>_<marker>_<business noun>` REQUIRED and checked; declaring nothing leaves the published DEFAULT in force, which still closes the role table but does not require the marker.

marker.description: The token that makes this bundle's served relations addressable as ITS OWN — commonly the source key carried by its descriptors' `metadata.source`, lowercased. This is what resolves the already-clean-noun case: when a raw relation is already a clean business noun there is no source-system infix to strip, so the served relation takes the marker instead of a name equal to the raw one. Required: a naming block without a marker declares nothing a gate can check.

roles.description: relation KIND -> how this bundle spells that kind's role prefix, and whether the marker is required in it. CLOSED on the kind (propertyNames enum), open on the spelling, because the kinds are a fact about what a served relation can BE while the prefix is the bundle's to choose. Omit to take the table in `default` below, which tools/check_served_name_distinct.py READS from here rather than restating — the enforced default and the published default are one object, so they cannot drift. Those defaults are measured, not invented: across the estate's served descriptors the leading token is `v` or `dim` or `meta` and NEVER `fact`, and the marker rides on the bundle-specific view names while the conformed dimensions go without it. The kind `fact` exists here precisely so the table can SAY that a served fact is spelled `v`: that is the one split the closed table settles, and it was left open by an ellipsis in the gate's prose until seven operators reading that prose independently disagreed about it.

prefix.description: The leading token every served relation of this kind carries, without its underscore.

marker.description: Whether `marker` must appear as a token of a name carrying this prefix. `required` is the honest setting for bundle-specific relations; `optional` for conformed ones whose name is shared by design. Defaults to `required`.

example.description: One worked raw->served rename, quoted VERBATIM by the gate at the point of failure. The failure message is the surface that measurably transmits a convention, so a bundle that has a better example than the derived one should put it here.

conformance.description: What this bundle declares about its own conformance. `out_of_scope` is the ONLY sanctioned escape from MAC001: a bundle may own files MAC does not define, provided it says which and why. Declared out of scope is honest; silently unchecked is not.

disclosure.description: WHAT THIS BUNDLE PERMITS TO BE PUBLISHED OUT OF ITS OWN DATA. A bundle-level POLICY statement, in the same idiom as `conformance.out_of_scope`: a claim plus the reason for it, made once, in the manifest, where a reader and a gate both find it — never per page and never per concept, because a per-page switch is a per-page mistake. Distinct from `capabilities` (what the container CAN do) and from `publish` (where output GOES): this says what the bundle's own rows are allowed to become. CLOSED (`additionalProperties: false`) so a second disclosure question is a schema change with a record rather than a key somebody adds on a Tuesday.

samples.description: MAY THE ROWS THEMSELVES BE RENDERED ON A GENERATED PAGE? The sampler (tools/mac_sample.py --plane concepts) draws a seeded random sample of each concept's MEMBERS into data/samples/concepts/. Whether those rows may be RENDERED to a reader — the console's Sample view, or any other surface that shows them — is this key's decision. The rendered concept page carries no rows: the operator ruled the sample belongs on its own view and not on the page, so the semantic page stays semantic. That is safe for a bundle over synthetic data and it is a data leak for a bundle over customer data — and the two bundles produce the SAME PAGE from the same code, so the difference cannot live in the projector. It lives here. DEFAULT WITHHELD, and a bundle that says nothing withholds: the harm is asymmetric (a withheld sample costs a reader one convenience; a published one cannot be recalled), and the measured shape is concrete — one live bundle's raw preview already trips the public-repo leak gate on a real organisation name, and the same page in a customer bundle would publish forty customer rows. WITHHOLDING IS NOT SILENCE: the page still renders the section, still says a sample exists, and still states the member count. Absent altogether, this key means withheld, which is why it is optional and why no bundle turns red for lacking it.

publish.description: `true` publishes the drawn member rows onto the generated concept pages. BOOLEAN, DELIBERATELY, AND THE READER CHECKS FOR `true` AND NOT FOR TRUTHINESS: `publish: "no"` is a truthy string in Python, and a disclosure gate a typo can open is not a gate. There is no per-concept override, and that is the design: an exception list is a place for the one row nobody re-read.

reason.description: WHY THESE ROWS MAY LEAVE THE BUNDLE — required when `publish` is true (see this object's `allOf`), and rendered ON the page under the sample, so the justification travels with the thing it justifies instead of staying in a manifest nobody opens. Not required for withholding: refusing to publish needs no defence, publishing does. Say what makes the data publishable (synthetic, licensed, already public), not who approved it.

seed.description: THE SEED THE SAMPLER DREW WITH, so a published sample is reproducible. Read by tools/mac_sample.py; admitted 2026-10-05 — the node is `additionalProperties: false`, so a bundle that set a seed its own sampler reads failed validation.

allOf.$comment: PUBLISHING IS THE CLAIM THAT NEEDS A BASIS. A bundle may withhold without a word, but the manifest line that turns forty rows of its data into a published page must say what makes that safe — the same shape conformance.out_of_scope already requires of its escape hatch, where `path` without `reason` is refused.

reproduction.description: How this bundle is rebuilt — as DATA, so a gate can check the artifacts still match the record. Prose cannot: <dataset>'s REPRODUCTION.md carried two stale claims simultaneously (a prohibition naming one of the two commands that trigger it, and a gate list naming three of eleven checkers, retired). Both read as authoritative.

allOf.$comment: v0.1.18: A HALF-MIGRATED RECORD MUST NOT READ AS COMPLETE. Declaring two pipelines and leaving a stage unassigned would let a manifest claim the split while the record could not say which pipeline half its stages ran in — the same failure shape as a narrative pointing at a missing file.

narrative.description: path to the human-readable twin, e.g. REPRODUCTION.md

pipelines.description: THE TWO PIPELINES, and the only place a reader of a day-zero bundle learns there are two. A bundle may declare a DATA pipeline and an ONTOLOGY pipeline, each with its own MANUALLY STARTED entry point, and the data pipeline's `exit` is not a produces-glob but A NAMED HUMAN'S SIGN-OFF. That one line is the whole governance ruling made checkable: the ontology pipeline may not start until a person has approved the dataset configuration. WHY A CORE KEY AND NOT AN EXTENSION: `^x-` was CLOSED in v0.1.14 and check_extension_keys refuses it as MAC012, and the measured lesson is exactly this case — x-grain held the grain, was unreachable by every gate, and two of four declarations rotted into false while still reading as VERIFIED. A declaration no gate can reach is worse than none. ADDITIVE AND OPTIONAL: a manifest without this key declares one pipeline, the two-pipeline gate does not apply to it, and its ontology plane stays governed by the operator's unlock marker exactly as before — so no existing bundle turns red. EXACTLY TWO PROPERTIES, additionalProperties false: a THIRD pipeline is then a schema change, which is a decision with a record, rather than a config value somebody adds on a Tuesday. Read by tools/check_data_plane_approved.py and by the ontology guard.

entry.description: the command an operator types to START this pipeline. Manual by rule: nothing chains into it.

the command an operator types to START the ontology pipeline. Independent in TRIGGER, in INPUTS and in FAILURE from the data pipeline — it needs no warehouse and no billed call — but NOT independent in TRUTH: see reproduction.pipelines.data.exit.

pipeline.description: the pipeline whose declared exit must be reached before this one may start.

WHICH of the two declared pipelines this stage belongs to. Required on EVERY stage once reproduction.pipelines is present (see the conditional below), so a half-migrated record cannot read as complete. READ by the console rather than inferred from the stage key: a page that guesses which pipeline a stage belongs to is a second home for a fact the manifest already states.

authoring.description: WHO authors this stage's outputs. `tool` = deterministic/mechanical (projection, scaffolding). `model` = an LLM authors them from live metadata + SME context — this is what 'harvest' MEANS, and it is NOT mechanical: the data-plane prompt asks a model to author descriptors, DQ findings, cleansing rules and view SQL. `hand` = a human or agent authors from business sources. `model-then-hand` = model draft, human refinement — the honest state of most harvested bundles. ADDED after `tool` was measured to be a false claim about the data plane on <dataset>: calling LLM authoring 'mechanical' is what lets 17 of 22 concepts carry an unreviewed CONFIRMED stamp without anyone noticing a claim had been made.

command.description: the command that performs it, when there is one

produces.description: bundle-relative globs this stage is expected to create

prohibited.description: Commands that must NOT be run against this bundle, each with the reason. A prohibition must name EVERY command that reaches the forbidden behaviour, not just the obvious one. USE SPARINGLY AND ONLY ON A RULING. A prohibition on the only mechanism that can produce an artifact does not protect the bundle — it guarantees that artifact is hand-written forever. A tool whose CURRENT output is inadequate is a limitation to record on the stage, not a ban.

gate.description: the command that decides whether the rebuild succeeded

acceptance.description: Where this source declares its test-verification artifacts for the generic board/gate.

lookups.description: data/lookups root — the value registers a concept may delegate to.

MigrationDecisionsFile.description: <bundle>/migration_decisions.yaml — the judgements behind a bundle's move to the column standard, keyed <Concept>.<column>: a role (and identity, measure, rulings) or an explicit `exclude`, each with `because`. Read by tools/mac_migrate_concepts.py --decisions. AI proposes it (--propose-decisions); a person ratifies it; it is kept so the migration is reproducible and arguable. Added 2026-09-29.

StandingFailuresFile.description: acceptance/standing_failures.yaml — the reds run_framework_gates.sh may carry for THIS bundle, each with an owner, a since, a reason and what makes it green. Read by tools/gate_register.py before every run (mac.gate_failures/1). Declared in guardrails/unfiled.yaml as `standing_failures` (authored-once: it is the decision to carry a red, not a measurement). Added 2026-09-29 — it was routed by location to PropertiesFile and refused the same hour it was declared.

scope.description: a bundle register carries bundle:<name>; repository-level reds live in the framework's tools/framework_gate_failures.yaml, never here

standing.description: MUST equal the number of entries — two statements of one size cannot drift

PropertiesFile.description: WAREHOUSE INVARIANTS — the L2 (execution-validated) evidence. Each property carries SQL that RUNS against the warehouse and asserts a fact the ontology's rules DEPEND on. This is not corpus testing (no questions, no answers) and no local check replaces it: an `examples`-style test exercises a canon in memory, while these ask whether the DATA still satisfies the assumption. An additivity property on <dataset> asserts a year decomposes into exactly 12 month-end buckets with no hidden roll-up row — if that stopped being true, every canon would still pass and every yearly figure would be silently inflated.

assertion.description: WHAT IS CLAIMED, and one claim only. Was an untyped object: three unrelated questions could be collapsed into a single must_be_zero and a reader could not tell WHICH claim broke. `type` is closed; `columns` names the projected columns carrying the verdict; `expect` is used only by `equals`. A property making several claims is several properties.

type.description: the closed set of pass/fail predicates the runner implements

columns.description: projected columns carrying the verdict; every one must be returned by `sql`

expect.description: `equals` only: column -> expected value. A measured value, dated in `source`.

tolerance.description: the band. Meaningless for must_be_zero; required by min_value/max_value.

validates.description: the CONCEPTS this property holds to account — the attribution link that makes L2 evidence usable. Without it a property passes and no concept learns anything: the suite proves the warehouse satisfies an assumption, but nothing records WHICH part of the model was thereby execution-validated, so FRAMEWORK.md §8's third rung cannot be measured for any object. Each entry is a concept.name. A property validating nothing is legal and means exactly that — a warehouse invariant no concept depends on, which is worth knowing. REQUIRED as of this generation: an artifact nobody tests is a claim. It was optional and stood unfilled on 0 of 59 properties.

test_kind.description: mac.test_kind.conformance | mac.test_kind.ground_truth. WHERE THE STANDARD COMES FROM, and the two have opposite obligations. conformance: every asserted value is RENDERED from a declaration at run time — a typed literal IS the defect. ground_truth: measures the world and must NOT be generated from the declaration's own claims, because its purpose is to disagree when the declaration is stale. A property that is both can be trusted for neither.

accepted.description: a dated, signed decision to live with a red. NOT a pass. Already honoured by the runner; given a shape here so it cannot be an unsigned note.

notes.description: a human note ON this property — why it is shaped as it is, what was changed and when. Distinct from `statement`, which says what the property PROVES: a reader needs the claim, a maintainer needs the history. Free prose, but the retired-vocabulary gate still reads it.

frozen.description: repair of this property is DEFERRED, and that is different from accepting its red. `accepted` says the finding is real and tolerated. `frozen` says nobody has judged the finding yet, because the property itself is scheduled for replacement — it hand-implements a rule the ontology is about to make machine-readable, so repairing it now would re-encode that rule BY HAND and then delete it. Two kinds of red that look identical on a board and mean opposite things. It exists because the alternative is worse: an untouched red drifts into being read as a known failure, and a repaired one costs the work twice. `until` names what unfreezes it, so a frozen property cannot quietly become permanent.

until.description: the condition that ends the freeze — normally the rule id whose conversion supersedes this property. A freeze with no exit is a deletion nobody agreed to.

verdict_from.description: the run whose verdict prompted the freeze, so a stale red is not mistaken for a fresh one

purpose.description: what this suite is FOR, in one paragraph a reader can act on. Authored, not generated.

generated_by.description: the tool that wrote this file, when nobody authored it. A generated suite that cannot name its generator is indistinguishable from a hand-written one that stopped being maintained.

PropertyItem.description: v0.5 CROSS-CLASS primitive — a concept property. Identical shape wherever `properties:` appears (reference / entity / event / measure): name + type + required + doc. Empirically uniform across 72/72 property items. The Palantir 'property'.

name.description: The property's name as the ontology states it. A property is an INTRINSIC PRIMITIVE attribute of this concept; anything pointing at another concept is an edge, not a property.

required.description: Whether every instance must carry this property. A claim about the NOTION, not about the current rows: a required property that is null in the data is a data-quality finding, and declaring it optional to make the finding go away is how a defect becomes invisible.

doc.description: What this property means, for a reader — what it records and at what grain. The one thing a type cannot say: `string` does not distinguish a name from a code from a free-text note.

value_domain.description: (optional) an enumeration this property's values must belong to

ProtoSqlFile.description: a DETERMINISTIC SQL FRAGMENT declared as data rather than prose. Exists because a recipe re-implemented from memory is got wrong: <dataset> records the same latest-vintage collapse being wrong FOUR TIMES IN ONE DAY by careful parties, once moving a figure by 25%. NOTE — the framework ships `mac.canon.*` for exactly this, so a fragment here is usually a workaround for a canon that is missing or broken, and the better fix is upstream.

ReferenceEndpoint.description: ONE END of a physical reference: a relation and a column, as two fields. Never a concept, and never a join string to be re-parsed.

ReferenceFile.description: how one relation REFERENCES others, MEASURED through the connector and written only by machine (tools/mac_references.py). One file per relation under data/references/. WHY IT IS ITS OWN FAMILY AND NOT AN ONTOLOGY EDGE. An ontology edge relates BUSINESS OBJECTS; a reference relates RELATIONS AND COLUMNS. They look alike and are not the same claim, and for a while one file carried both: physical entries keyed by `endpoints.from.concept` with the relations and columns flattened into a `join_rule` string. The consequences were measured — a bundle with no ontology could draw no physical diagram at all, crow's feet were authored claims rather than measurements, and a reference whose two columns are spelled differently was unreachable because a concept-keyed entry is written by somebody who already believes the two things are one thing. A reference here is therefore keyed by RELATION AND COLUMN as FIELDS on both ends. The words `concept`, `edge` and `join_rule` do not appear in this family and tools/check_physical_references.py fails a file that reintroduces them. CARDINALITY AND PARTICIPATION ARE TWO BLOCKS because they are two claims from two different measurements. Keys alone draw every relationship mandatory; participation is the half a key cannot supply. A human editing this file is a MAC002 error.

metadata.description: carries schema_version so the validator does not SKIP this file. A skipped file is an unvalidated one, which for a machine-written plane is the whole risk.

of.description: the CHILD relation stem every entry in this file is keyed by. A references file whose descriptor is gone measures nothing.

measurement.description: WHAT WAS IN SCOPE, so no count in this file can be read without its denominator. `relations_in_scope` and `parent_endpoints` are the population the candidate space was generated from; `key_source` names where the parent keys were READ (they are never re-derived here — two answers to 'what is the key' is the drift the plane exists to prevent). Carries NO CLOCK on purpose: the per-relation file is byte-identical across runs over unchanged data and the measurement time lives in the run record it names.

admission.description: EVERY NUMBER A VERDICT TURNS ON, repeated in every file it judges. A reader opens ONE file, and an entry whose verdict depends on a floor must not be readable without that floor. Nothing that decides a verdict may live only in a Python constant: the inclusion-only version of this measurement admitted a demographic column as a reference to a product key at 1.000000 over 104,990 rows, and the reviewer who would have caught it could not see the rule.

references.description: the measured references this relation carries. `drawn: false` means real and superseded by a stronger parent — recorded, not deleted.

references_dangling.description: columns that follow this bundle's OWN key-naming convention, are not keys, and have NO parent relation in scope. `to` is null and that is the class: the moment a dangling reference acquires a parent it is a claim, and claims are measured. Reported, never invented and never dropped.

candidates_rejected.description: WHAT WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED, with its numbers. An operator who cannot see this cannot tell a missing reference from an unconsidered one.

references_broken.description: References too aligned with a key to be coincidence and too broken to draw — measured between `broken_reference_floor` and `near_miss_floor` with the parent's key domain exercised. NOT DRAWN, RAISED: the ER model must not show a line the rows disobey, and each entry carries a prepared ruling (CORE.md §6). Added v0.1.15 with the band itself.

items.description: v0.5: render_kind is REQUIRED. The 'formula' family was dropped → use template/logic (DROP→template).

then.$comment: an injected rule must carry its canonical SQL template
a view-backed rule must reference the pre-deposited view

ShapesFile.description: DOMAIN shape invariants, held per-source and deliberately OUT of the framework's universal mac_shapes.yaml so the framework stays domain-pure. Same grammar as the universal shapes; different scope and different owner.

SmeLedgerFile.description: THE DOUBT CHANNEL. A harvest with nowhere to put an uncertainty writes it out as a confident fact — measured on a bundle that had no ledger: 17 of 22 concepts arrived stamped confidence C with an owner who had never seen them, and one unreviewed claim produced a wrong value anchor that stood for weeks. An OPEN QUESTION is a successful outcome of authoring, and this is where it goes.

TableFile.description: A DATASET OR SOURCE DESCRIPTOR. `foreign_keys:` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT (removed 2026-10-05; operator ruling 2026-09-27). A foreign key is declared ON THE COLUMN — `columns[].role: foreign_key` plus `columns[].references`, a mapping carrying `to` with `cardinality` and `participation` PER SIDE (child and parent). That is strictly MORE than the retired table-level block could state: it had one `cardinality_at_to` and no participation at all, which is why the ER diagram could not be drawn from it. Measured over the 16 delivered descriptors: 0 wrote the block, 18 columns carry `role: foreign_key` and 23 carry `references`. The block was not merely unused — it was ACTIVELY HARMFUL: tools/mac_model.py read it and nothing else, so the shared model reported ZERO foreign keys on every delivered bundle while 18 sat on the columns beside it. That reader now takes the column form first and the block only as a fallback, as its five siblings already did; those fallbacks stay, so an unmigrated bundle still resolves even though the schema no longer admits the key.

kind.description: WHICH OF THE TWO HOMES THIS DESCRIPTOR DESCRIBES — the raw schema-of-record under `data/sources/`, or the served relation under `data/datasets/`. They are ONE shape: identical `table.*` and `columns[].*`, so this key is the whole difference. It was `{type: string}` with no enum and no description until 2026-10-05, which made the single discriminator of the data plane an open field. `external: true` sat beside it as a second marker and is removed: the generator could only ever emit it inside `if not served`, so it was present-or-absent typed as a boolean, it was read by nothing, and it said what this key already says.

observed.description: the date the measurement was taken

status.description: A LIFECYCLE FACT ABOUT THE FILE, NOT A GRADE OF THE MEASUREMENT. `retired` is read by check_datasets_are_grounded, which skips a descriptor whose relation is gone — the one real consumer. `draft` is NOT permitted: a measurement is not a draft, it either happened or it did not, and every generated descriptor was born `draft` for no reader at all.

metadata.description: CLOSED v0.1.15. It was an open object — `additionalProperties` unset and `properties` empty — so it accepted any key, and that is the hatch `status: draft` and `confidence: I` came through while the column object beside it was strictly closed. `table` REMOVED 2026-10-05: it duplicated `table.name` in 16 of 16 descriptors, and the FILENAME too — a triple. It had zero readers (the one hit was a writer), and the filename<->table.name link is already enforced by tools/check_relation_identity.py, so the fact was policed twice over without this third copy.

rows_measured.description: MEASURED row count at `metadata.observed`. Written by mac_descriptors and READ by its own --check, which reports DRIFT when the warehouse no longer agrees.

table.description: A MEASUREMENT CARRIES NO GRADE OF BELIEF. `confidence` was a core key on this object and NOTHING read it there — every reader in the framework reads confidence on an ONTOLOGY artifact (concept metadata, enumeration members, rules, edges). CONFORMANCE.md §2 step 2 is the test it failed: 'an agent or projector reads it directly — a key nothing consumes is a note, and a note belongs in prose.' Asserting 'inferred' about a type read out of information_schema is not inference. Removed v0.1.15; the two planes that already carried no belief (profiles, references) were the ones getting it right.

derived_from.description: (views only) LINEAGE — how this serving relation is built. Absent for base tables. For engineers/governance + rebuild; NOT read by the query-generating agent (the concept grounds to the relation agnostically).

sources.description: the raw/upstream relation(s) this view is built from

bakes_out.description: the impurities/workarounds this view dissolves (the homologation payoff)

distinct.description: MEASURED distinct value count. Written by mac_lookups when the captured `values:` list is cut into a register, and READ by the generated data-sanity suite and by the dangling-key ruling. It replaced the member list itself: 1,186 of 1,595 descriptor lines were member lists, 563 of them on one column that no register would take.

key_position.description: THIS COLUMN'S PLACE IN A COMPOSITE PRIMARY KEY — 1 for the first part, 2 for the second. Present only on a key column of a multi-column key; absent on a single-column key. IT REPLACES THE ROLE `composite_key_part`, by operator ruling 2026-09-27. That term carried MEMBERSHIP and no ORDER, so the order of a composite key lived only in the concept plane's `key: [...]` list — a second home for a fact that belongs to the RELATION. Worse, splitting the key across two role terms meant a consumer asking 'what is this relation's key' had to remember both, and two did not: mac_to_graph.py:35 and mac_to_shacl.py:129 test `role == 'primary_key'` and therefore found NO key at all for the reference bundle's fact table, whose two key columns both carried `composite_key_part`. WHY A NUMBER AND NOT `primary_key_1` / `primary_key_2`, which the operator proposed and then accepted the argument against: an ordinal inside a categorical token has to be parsed out by every consumer that wants to sort by it — the same shape as StoreCode = StoreKey // 10, a value encoded in an identifier. As an integer it compares and sums; as a suffix it is string surgery in N places. Checked by the KEY-POSITION invariant: the positions on one relation are exactly 1..n, no gaps, no repeats, and none on a column that is not a key.

references.description:
The parent this column points at. TWO SHAPES, both read by one resolver (`mac_project.column_reference`): * a STRING `relation.column` — the original form, all a page's reference cell ever needed; * a MAPPING carrying `to` plus the measured `cardinality` and `participation`.
The mapping exists so the ER DIAGRAM is constructable FROM THE DESCRIPTOR. It previously read `data/references*/` for every relationship while the page read this field, which is two homes for "is this a foreign key" — Measured, the diagram drew 17 relationships measured on a worked bundle while the pages listed 6. Cardinality and participation are the crow's feet and `er_model.py` calls them "the half a key cannot supply", so the picture cannot be drawn without them.
WHAT DOES NOT BELONG HERE: the evidence. `admitted_because`, the thirteen `evidence` counters, `ambiguous_with` and `needs_ruling` stay on MeasuredReference in `data/references*/`, where they were measured. This field says WHAT THE RELATIONSHIP IS; that artifact says WHY IT IS TRUE. Copying the second into the first is not one home, it is two copies.
Written by mac_descriptors from a measured reference whose `parent_key_role` is `identity` and whose cardinality is many:one — never from a column-name coincidence, because a foreign key between two tables may have entirely different column names on its two ends.

cardinality.description: MEASURED cardinality. `child` is how many rows of the referencing relation relate to one row of the parent; `parent` the converse. An identity parent is `one`; a key PART is `many`, because a shared value domain is not an identifying join.

participation.description: MEASURED participation — the half a key cannot supply. `parent: optional` means some parent rows are referenced by NO child row; `child: optional` means some child rows carry no parent. Without it an optional relationship and a mandatory one draw the same crow's foot wherever nobody thought about it.

register.description: Path to the register that holds this column's members, relative to the bundle root. Written by mac_lookups, READ by check_register_membership, which re-measures those members against the warehouse — the monitor a closed set is owed (DNA 1.8).

role.description: v0.5 (DECISION 4): the canonical PHYSICAL role set is kept. An applied ontology's analytical roles (mac_vocabulary.yaml#concept.column.role: key/dimension/measure/period/housekeeping — `attribute` is retired) are mapped down to this during projection; they do NOT enter the schema. 'unknown' is forbidden in production-status files (enforced separately). v0.1.14 (C1): 'delivery_axis' added — a column that splits ROWS without splitting FIGURES, measured by mac_admit_identity.py. This does NOT reopen DECISION 4: the barred roles are the ontology's ANALYTICAL ones (the five of mac_vocabulary.yaml#concept.column.role), whereas the enum already carries identity-participation roles (primary_key, foreign_key, composite_key_part) and 'delivery_axis' is the measured COMPLEMENT of composite_key_part. A column left 'unknown' while the admission test reports it COLLAPSIBLE is the residue awaiting a human ruling — and 'unknown' is already forbidden in production-status files, so no new gate is needed.

searchable.description: HOW A VALUE IN THIS COLUMN IS RESOLVED when no register can hold it. The operator, 2026-09-29: "not everyting is suitable for lookup. one huge table where the search criteria is text cannot be converted into lookup. it should just be declared later to be searchebal with like." Written by mac_descriptors from mac_register_plan.classify — the same rule the planner is tested against, imported rather than restated — and READ by the relation page, which prints `search: like` in the reference cell. Before it, an open-text column carried nothing there and was indistinguishable from one nobody had profiled: a worked bundle held 16, including dim_customer.customer_name at 99,200 distinct over 104,990 rows. Mutually exclusive with `register` by construction, since the rule is only consulted where a column has none.

values.description: TRANSIENT — the measured bounded domain, on its way to a register. NOT A HOME. `mac_profile` writes it; `mac_lookups` cuts it into data/lookups/, points the column at it with `register:`, and POPS this key. A DELIVERED descriptor must therefore carry no `values:` at all, which is enforced by the DOMAIN-HOMED invariant in check_delivery_consistency — the operator ruled the member lists out of the YAML on 2026-09-26 ("these values could be in lookup if necessary?!?!", and the move cut the descriptor plane by 73 %) and asked on 2026-09-28 whether anything made the ruling stick: nothing did. Compliance was an accident of stage ORDERING — measured that day, a worked bundle 0 of 14 and a worked bundle 0 of 16 were clean only because `mac_descriptors` happened to run last, while a worked bundle carried member lists on 7 of 7 source descriptors, one of them 120 members long. It stays in the schema because the hand-off is real and a producer must be able to write a valid file mid-pipeline; what is forbidden is SURVIVING to delivery.

items.description: A MEASUREMENT CARRIES NO GRADE OF BELIEF. `confidence` was a core key on this object and NOTHING read it there — every reader in the framework reads confidence on an ONTOLOGY artifact (concept metadata, enumeration members, rules, edges). CONFORMANCE.md §2 step 2 is the test it failed: 'an agent or projector reads it directly — a key nothing consumes is a note, and a note belongs in prose.' Asserting 'inferred' about a type read out of information_schema is not inference. Removed v0.1.15; the two planes that already carried no belief (profiles, references) were the ones getting it right.

role.description: descriptive reverse-pointer role (e.g. primary_table, referenced, discriminator_column) — free text, not a load-bearing controlled vocabulary.

TransformFile.description: DATA-PLANE pipeline descriptor (two-plane layout, data/transforms/). Declares how ONE produced dataset is built: what it `produces`, the `inputs` it consumes (each typed by `kind`), and the ordered cleansing `transforms`. The realizing SQL lives beside it (produces.sql_file). Read by lineage/rebuild tooling and the lineage projection; NOT by the query-generating agent (a concept grounds to the produced relation agnostically). Distinguished from a TableFile by its `produces`+`inputs` discriminators.

because.description: WHAT MOTIVATED IT — a data-quality finding id, for `proposed` and `ruled`. A proposal without its finding is an opinion, and the point of proposing is that the measurement is already on record: DQ-DUP-ORDERROWS-SALES is why only one of two identical 223,974-row relations is served. Read from a `-- mac.transform.because:` line in the.sql.
